governing: shear_rupture of the bracket plate on the net section through the bolt line nearest the load (Anv = (18.5 - 6 x 7/8) x 3/8 = 4.97 in2, Rn/Omega = 96.9 kip)
notes: ASD, Ra = 88.107 kip at e = 6 in. Bolts: 12 x 3/4 in Group 150 (A490-N), 6 rows x 2 columns, s = 3 in, g = 5.5 in (the W12x65 workable gauge), standard holes, snug-tight; ICR C = 7.387, Ra/(C rn/Omega) = 88.107/110.9 = 0.79 (elastic-method cross-check 0.98). Per-bolt bearing and tearout on the plate (Lev = Leh = 1-3/4 in) and on the column flange all exceed the bolt shear strength, so bolt shear sets the group strength. Plate (3/8 in A572 Gr 50, 18-1/2 in tall): shear yield 0.64, shear rupture 0.91, block shear 0.55; flexural yield, flexural rupture, F11 lateral-torsional buckling and Part 9/10 plate buckling all pass even with the moment arm taken conservatively as the full 6 in (worst 0.83, plate buckling); shear-flexure yield interaction 0.71. Spacing, edge distances (min and max) and flange fit meet J3.3-J3.5. The same layout with Group 120 threads-included (A325-N) bolts would sit at exactly 1.00 on bolt shear, so do not substitute A325-N; A325-X with threads verified out of the shear plane is equivalent. The plate must extend past the 6 in load line to pick up the load; the column itself (member, flange and web under the bracket moment) is outside this connection check.
